newsitem.title: CHINA: China Jan-Feb industrial output up 10.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: China Jan-Feb industrial output up 10.4 pct.

text.p: China's industrial output for the first two months of 1997 was up 10.4 percent over the same period last year, the State Statistical Bureau said on Tuesday.
It said industrial output value rose 12.1 percent year on year adjusted for seasonal holiday factors, however.
The State Statistical Bureau said total output value was 278.7 billion yuan ($33.5 billion) for the period.
China had previously announced industrial output rose 10.3 percent in January.

In the January-February period, wholly owned state industry showed a rise in output value of 4.6 percent while collective industry posted an increase of 10.5 percent and the private sector, which includes many foreign joint ventures, was up 15.8 percent.
Light industry rose 10.9 pecent during the two-month period while heavy industry registered a 10 percent gain.

Output of durables such as refrigerators, washing machines and air-conditioners rose 11-21.8 percent over the period. Textile output declined overall with silk and knitted silk goods falling as much as 30.2 percent.
Primary energy production during the period was up 4.2 percent while coal output climbed 5.1 percent, electric power generation gained 4.4 percent and crude oil rose 1 percent.
The ratio of goods that were sold to those produced was 93.19 percent, up 1.07 percentage points from the same period last year.
Officials of the State Statistical Bureau said that only the total figure for output -- and not those for various sectors -- were adjusted for the Chinese New Year holiday, which fell in February.
Industrial output during the period was described by the bureau as stable but it added that enterprises still encountered problems with tight liquidity and low efficiency.
